exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Transpose of a Matrix

question.text:
If
    $
    {T} = 
    \left\lbrack
    \matrix {
        6 & -2\\
        0 & 3\\
        -5 & 4
    }
    \right\rbrack
    $,
then find the transpose of ${T}.$
question.explanation:
To find the transpose, we interchange the rows and columns:

\[ {T}^T = \left\lbrack \matrix { \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{6} & \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0} & \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-5} \\ \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-2} & \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{3} & \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{4} } \right\rbrack \]

exampleAnswers.title: Determining the Dimensions of the Transpose of a Matrix

question.explanation:
When a matrix is transposed, its dimensions switch from $m \times n$ to $n \times m.$

So, since ${Z}$ is a $6 \times 7$ matrix, the transpose ${Z}^T$ is a $\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{7} \times \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{6} $ matrix.

example.title: Determining the Dimensions of the Transpose of a Matrix

question.text:
Consider the matrix
  \[
    {A} = 
    \left\lbrack
    \matrix {
        7 & 2 & -1 & 5 & 0 \\
        4 & 8 & 3 & -6 & 1 \\
    }
    \right\rbrack.
    \]
What are the dimensions of $A^T?$
question.explanation:
When a matrix is transposed, its dimensions switch from $m \times n$ to $n \times m.$

So, since ${A}$ is a $2 \times 5$ matrix, the transpose ${A}^T$ is a $\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{5} \times \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{2} $ matrix.
